newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA should welcome transport wage ruling - Reith.
newsitem.headline: RBA should welcome transport wage ruling - Reith.

text.p: Australian Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said on Thursday that he expected the Reserve Bank of Australia, which is concerned about wage levels, to welcome the rejection of a wage rise sought by the main transport union.
"I would think the decision would be welcomed by the Reserve Bank," Reith told reporters when asked if the ruling earlier Thursday should ease the central bank's conerns about rising wages.
Australia's main labour court, the Industrial Relations Commission, on Thursday rejected an 11 percent wage claim by the powerful Transport Workers' Union.
Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane said earlier on Thursday that recent data on wages growth had been a setback to prospects for improving inflation.
The Liberal-National government, in its budget for the fiscal year from July 1, projected underlying inflation of two percent, year average, in 1997/89, unchanged from 1996/97.
It also forecast wages growth to average four percent.

Macfarlane told a business luncheon in Melbourne that the central bank's decision to cut official cash rates by a total of 150 basis points in the final six months of calendar 1996 was based on an assessment of improving prospects for inflation and the associated scope for additional economic growth.
"We would like to have seen that pattern of news continue, but the latest data on wages seems to have been a setback to that expectation," he said.

The latest official data on average weekly ordinary time earnings for full-time employees showed stronger than expected growth of 1.3 percent in the three months to February, taking annual growth to 4.6 percent and into the 4.5 to 5.0 percent zone which the RBA has expressed concerns about in the past.
